item.title: Fairlife Ransomware Halt, Windows LegacyHive Zero-Day, and EU Android AI Access Order
item.content:encoded:
New Windows LegacyHive zero-day gives hackers admin privileges — Must Read

A researcher released a proof-of-concept for a new Windows zero-day called LegacyHive that can let standard users gain admin-level code execution by abusing the Windows User Profile Service. The public PoC is intentionally limited and requires extra credentials, but experts confirmed it works and detection guidance is already available.

  • A security researcher using the handle Nightmare Eclipse released a proof-of-concept exploit called LegacyHive for a Windows zero-day in the Windows User Profile Service.
  • The LegacyHive proof of concept was published hours after Microsoft’s July 2026 Patch Tuesday updates and had not yet received a CVE ID at the time of the article.
  • Nightmare Eclipse said the released proof of concept was stripped down to require another standard user’s credentials and a third username, making it harder to weaponize publicly.
  • Will Dormann tested the exploit and said successful exploitation could let non-admin users modify the classes registry hive and gain automatic code execution when an administrator account logs into a compromised system.
  • Kevin Beaumont confirmed the exploit works and published Microsoft Defender for Endpoint detection queries for LegacyHive exploitation.

Dairy company Fairlife suspends production in US after cyber incident — Should Read

A ransomware attack forced Coca-Cola’s Fairlife dairy unit to temporarily halt production at its U.S. operations, though the company says product quality and safety were not affected. The scope of the incident remains under investigation, with law enforcement notified.

  • A ransomware attack forced Coca-Cola Company’s Fairlife dairy unit to temporarily halt production in the United States.
  • Coca-Cola said Fairlife detected the intrusion on Thursday and that the full scope of the incident is not yet known.
  • Coca-Cola said product quality and safety have not been impacted, and Fairlife’s operations in Canada were not affected.
  • Coca-Cola said an internal investigation is ongoing and law enforcement has been notified.
  • Coca-Cola did not identify the ransomware group behind the incident or announce any breach of corporate or consumer information.

E.U. Orders Google to Open Android Mic, Camera and Screen to Rival AI Assistants — Should Read

The European Commission ordered Google to open powerful Android AI-assistant capabilities, including access to the microphone, camera, screen, wake words, and app control, to rival assistants by Android 18 or August 2027. The move aims to curb Google’s gatekeeping under the Digital Markets Act, but it raises significant security and privacy concerns because third-party assistants could gain deep access to sensitive device data.

  • The European Commission ordered Google to give rival AI assistants the same Android access that Gemini has, including the camera, microphone, screen contents, always-on wake word, and background app control, in Android 18 or by 1 August 2027 at the latest.
  • The Android decision covers 11 operating system features, with Google allowed to require certification for five restricted features but barred from restricting access to six others, including ambient data, always-on hotword detection, long-press invocation, on-device models, third-party model implementation, and background execution.
  • For the restricted features, Google must create a Qualified AI Assistant Programme, accept certifications from third-party Trusted Certification Authorities, and apply the same conditions to Gemini.
  • The Commission also ordered Google to share anonymised Search query, click, and ranking data with rival search engines and AI chatbots that perform search, subject to eligibility rules, contracts, audits, and a cost-based fee.
  • Google objected that the Android decision threatens device security by granting external apps sensitive permissions, and the article notes that third-party assistants could gain access to notifications, SMS, screen contents, and screenshots.

Armenia Detains Russian Tourist on U.S. Warrant for REvil Hacker, Lawyers Say Wrong Man — Should Read

Armenia detained a Russian tourist named Aleksandr Ermakov on a U.S. extradition warrant for a REvil ransomware suspect, but his lawyers say authorities have mistaken him for a different Aleksandr Ermakov who is already serving a sentence in Russia. The case appears to hinge on identity confusion around incomplete name data in sanctions or Interpol records.

  • Armenia has detained Russian tourist Aleksandr Yuryevich Ermakov since June 28 on a U.S. extradition request for a REvil ransomware suspect named Aleksandr Ermakov.
  • The defense says the U.S. is seeking Aleksandr Gennadievich Ermakov, who was sanctioned by Australia, the United States, and the United Kingdom in January 2024 over the Medibank Private data theft.
  • Lawyers for the detained man say he is from Omsk, is a former prison-service lawyer, does not speak English, and is not the same person as the sanctioned hacker suspect.
  • Russian reporting cited in the article says the wanted Aleksandr Gennadievich Ermakov is serving a two-year Russian sentence for co-writing SugarLocker and is barred from leaving Russia.
  • The detained man is being held on a 30-day Interpol detention order while Armenian authorities have made no public statement and Moscow seeks consular access.

Three Brands, One Lure: A Chase 'Secure Message via Virtru' That Actually Came From LinkedIn — May Read

A phishing email impersonated a Chase secure message via Virtru while actually using a LinkedIn sender address and Mimecast-wrapped links, creating a three-brand mismatch designed to look trustworthy. The key warning sign was that the visible brand, sender, and link destination did not align, alongside stale and generic message content.

  • A phishing email impersonated Chase with a secure-message template that claimed the recipient had a new secure message via Virtru.
  • The email’s visible Chase branding, claimed Virtru provider, and actual From header of messages-noreply@linkedin.com created three unrelated identities in one message.
  • The call-to-action buttons used real Mimecast URL-protection domains, including a link with a chase.com parameter, instead of pointing directly to Chase.
  • The message contained signs of reused canned content, including an already-expired notice, broken grammar, and a generic ACH_Incoming_Payments label with no personalization.
  • IRONSCALES Themis classified the message as phishing at 90% confidence and remediated it across the affected mailboxes.

Zelensky appoints Ukraine's acting security service chief as acting defense minister — May Read

Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelensky appointed acting SBU chief Yevhenii Khmara as acting defense minister after a controversial reshuffle that sparked protests. Some lawmakers questioned whether the appointment is legal because Ukraine’s defense minister is required to be a civilian.

  • Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky appointed Yevhenii Khmara, the acting head of the Security Service of Ukraine, as acting defense minister.
  • Zelensky said he would formally ask parliament to approve Khmara as defense minister once the required legal procedures had been completed.
  • The appointment followed public anger and protests after Zelensky dismissed Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov earlier in the week.
  • Khmara previously led the SBU's Alpha Special Operations Center, which is responsible for counterterrorism operations, intelligence support, and some long-range strikes against Russian targets.
  • Several Ukrainian lawmakers questioned whether Khmara's appointment complied with Ukrainian law requiring the defense minister and deputy defense ministers to be civilians rather than serving military officers.

The Race to Field Military Autonomy Is On, Can Trusted Information Infrastructure Keep Pace? — Optional

Everfox argues that as the U.S., UK, and NATO accelerate military autonomy, the key challenge is building trusted information infrastructure that lets autonomous systems, AI tools, and coalition partners securely share mission data at speed. The article promotes hardware-enforced separation and cross-domain information sharing as the foundation for connected autonomous defense operations.

  • Military forces in the U.S., UK, and NATO are under increasing pressure to field autonomous capabilities faster through new investment, evolving defense strategies, and accelerated acquisition pathways.
  • The article argues that autonomous aircraft, uncrewed maritime vessels, ground systems, satellites, and AI-enabled mission applications require trusted information infrastructure to move telemetry, ISR, command data, AI outputs, sensor-to-shooter workflows, and coalition intelligence across platforms, domains, and partners.
  • Programs adopting commercial technologies through rapid acquisition and iterative delivery models need trusted information infrastructure designed from the outset to move mission information securely across platforms, classifications, and coalition environments.
  • The article describes hardware-enforced separation as an approach that establishes trust within hardware logic rather than relying solely on software controls, reducing architecture complexity by removing the operating system from the trust boundary.
  • Everfox presents its trusted information platform as a way for defense organizations to securely exchange mission-critical information across systems, classifications, and partners for autonomous and coalition missions.
